Title: Development of an exploratory taxonomy of veterinary AI query types and stage-specific query preferences: an expert panel study
Authors: Huh, C.; Huh, H.; Ahn, J.; Park, M.
Abstract: Background/objectives: The integration of large language model (LLM)-based AI tools into veterinary clinical practice is rapidly increasing; however, veterinary-specific frameworks for organizing AI query types and examining stage-specific preferences remain limited. This study aimed to develop an exploratory taxonomy of veterinary AI query types and to characterize veterinarians' stage-specific query preferences through a structured expert-panel survey. Methods: Candidate query types were drafted with the assistance of a locally deployed LLM from a preliminary review of de-identified veterinary AI chatbot query logs and refined through literature review. In a structured online survey, 43 veterinarians then selected the Clinical Support query types (A-H) they would prefer to direct to AI at each of five clinical stages and indicated preferred response formats; the survey measured self-reported query preferences, not observed use. Results: A taxonomy of 3 categories and 21 subtypes was established: Clinical Support Queries (Types A-H), Evidence-Based Research Queries (Types I-L), and Terminology and Drug Reference Queries (Types M-U). Across stages, Type B (Differential Reasoning) was most often ranked first (64/213 first-choice responses), and Type D (Clinical Decision Support) was most often ranked first for the post-consultation stage (21/42, 50.0%). In analyses accounting for repeated measures using generalized estimating equations, respondents with >=10 years of experience more often ranked Type G (Evidence Search) first than those with <10 years (OR 3.09, 95% CI 1.11-8.59; unadjusted p = 0.031), but this contrast was not significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across four contrasts (adjusted p = 0.062).
